Title: Speech at the opening of the conference on development issues in Burundi
CentralBank: Bank of the Republic of Burundi
text: Speech of the Governor of the BRB at the Conference on the "Development Issue in Burundi", scheduled for August 20, 2021 ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- Your Excellency the President of theRepublic; Honourable Members; Prime Minister; Members of the Government; Honourable Vice-Governors; Ladies and Gentlemen Administrators and Chief Executive Officers of Credit Institutions; Madam Resident Representative of the World Bank Group in Burundi; Dear Development Partners and Friends of Burundi; Ladies and Gentlemen, Distinguished Guests, any protocol observed; On this historic and important day for the Bank of the Republic of Burundi, it is anhonor and an immense joy for us to be honored in this room by You, Your Excellency the President of the Republic, for this event that the Bank of the Republic of Burundi will register in its assets with regard to exchanges on such a relevant subject that is "the Problem of Development in Burundi" focused mainly on on "Transforming untapped economic potential into effective, sustainable and inclusive economic growth". Your Excellency the President of the Republic, before getting to the heart of this subject that brings us together, allow me to begin by thanking God Almighty who, having still lent us life and kept usuntil this day, has granted us the chance to have You, Your Excellency the President of the Republic, among us at this high-level conference. On behalf of the Bank of the Republic of Burundi and on my own behalf, allow me, Your Excellency the President of theRepublic, to express our sincere thanks for having agreed that the Central Bank organizes this activity under the auspices of the Bank. Your Excellency's Patronage, despite the fact that time is very precious and constraining to You, because of yourmultiple commitments. We are thus delighted, Your Excellency the President of the Republic, that you have chosen to be physically present at this conference, because, as Commander of the Development of Burundi our dear Fatherland, You havealso shown your interest in following very closely, as is your custom, Your Excellency the President of the Republic, relevant issues of continuing concern to economic and sectoral policy makers, managers and beneficiaries. Your Excellency the President of the Republic, this conference will be moderated by eminent economists and sons of Burundi evolving outside the country but who always think of their homeland. He was joinedby Distinguished Professor Leonce Ndikumana, lecturer at the University of Massachusetts in the United States of America and Dr Janvier Desire Nkurunziza, Expert of the United Nations Conference on Trade and Development, UNCTAD in Acronym, based inGeneva. Your Excellency, Mr President of the Republic, development being a rather complex process, it refers to all the structural transformations that make possible and accompany economic growth and the raising ofliving standards, everyone can testify that as I do that this is at the centre of your concerns, Your Excellency Mr President of the Republic. In addition to the financing aspects, these structural transformations also covereconomic, social, demographic, mental and even political dimensions. It follows from this definition that the question of development concerns, or better still, involves various actors who must interact in harmony and perfect coordination on at least four dimensions which converge in terms of sectors: the public and the private on theone hand, and the internal and external on the other. It is on this basis that we have invited the various actors to this conference, taking these dimensions into account. Presentations focused on the theme You announced,Excellence Mr. Chairman, we understand that the discussions and conclusions can give a clear enough impetus to better understand, among other things, the potential for economic growth in Burundi, the challenges and constraints of development in Burundi, the problem of financing development in Burundi, the link between the various macroeconomic and sectoral policies as well as possible solutions to ensure development materialized by sustained and inclusive growth, in accordance with the strategic orientations that the Government says Laborious and Responsible has already set itself. Thus, aware of the stakes, opportunities and challenges of sustainable development, on the one hand, and referring to the challenges related to the promotion of economic growth in Burundi, on theother hand, the Bank of the Republic of Burundi has introduced, since 2019, new measures to support, through appropriate refinancing mechanisms, credit institutions, here banksand microfinance institutions, in order to encourage them to support more financing for growth sectors. Similarly, given that the contribution and dynamics of the private sector are crucial to the successof development in general and economic growth in particular, this policy has been pursued and systematically adjusted, and this shows that the Central Bank is aware that, in addition to preserving price stability and the financial system, it must also contribute to the implementation of economic policies conducive to the harmonious development of the country, with particular emphasis on the development of the private sector. It is in this perspective that the Central Bank has always maintained a permanent exchange with the banking and microfinance sector, but also, in a certain way, measure, with economic operators who wish to invest in projects and sectors of visible socio-economic importance. Your Excellency the President of the Republic, the Central Bank is aware that there are many challenges for the maximum success of this policy, but it remains committed to strengthening exchanges with the various stakeholders and to playing a leading role, particularly with regard to the revitalization of the macroeconomic and sectoral policy coordination framework, in order to ensure that activities in the various sectors of the economy concerned by economic policy are better linked, namely the production and prices sector, the external sector, the public finance and debt sector and the monetary sector. This is because macroeconomic and sectoral policies must be articulated in strict coherence of instruments, and monetary policy must play a highly complementary role to that of fiscal policy, as the main tools for managing macroeconomic policy. Your Excellency the President of theRepublic, returning to the heart of the subject that brings us together during today's conference, we hope that the presentations and exchanges that will result from it will enable us to better identify, among other things, the economic growth potential of Burundi, the challenges and constraints of development in Burundi, the problem of financing for development, the interactions and coherence of the various instruments for managing macroeconomic and sectoral policies and the worstsolutions for achieving harmonious development of the Burundian economy. It is with these wishes that I would like to submit to Your Excellency, the official opening of this Conference, whose relevance of the debates and recommendations for the development of the Burundian economy we are already anticipating. Thank you, Your Excellency the President of the Republic.

Title: Opening speech of the Governor, Dieudonn MURENGERANTWARI to the 26th ordinary meeting of the EAC Monetary Affairs Committee held at Bujumbura on 17th of March, 2023
CentralBank: Bank of the Republic of Burundi
text: P.O. Box 1096 ARUSHA, TANZANIA Tel: 255-27-2162100/14 Fax: 255-27-2162102/2162191 E-mail: eac@eachq.org Web: 26TH ORDINARY MEETING OF THE MONETARY AFFAIRS COMMITTEE 13TH to 17TH MARCH 2023 OPENING REMARKS BY THE CHAIR OF MAC, THE GOVERNOR OF THE BRB Honourable Dr Patrick Njoroge, Governor of Central Bank of Kenya; Honourable Emmanuel Tutuba, Governor of Bank of Tanzania; Honourable Dr Michael Antingi-Ego, Deputy Governor of Bank of Uganda; Honourable John RWANGOMBWA, Governor National Bank of Rwanda; Honourable Johnny Ohisa Damian, Governor Bank of South Soudan; Honourable Steven Mlote, Deputy Secretary General of EAC; Dear Senior Officials Members of the Monetary Affairs Committee; Distinguished Delegates, Ladies and Gentlemen. All Protocol observed; Good Morning Thank you to each and every one of you for being here with us today. It is my honour and great pleasure to welcome you all to the twenty-sixth ordinary meeting of the Monetary Affairs Committee. We thank you for your presence here in Bujumbura, and we hope you had safe trip and have enjoyed so far the good weather and the Burundian hospitality. Honourable Governors, Ladies and Gentlemen, Distinguished Delegates I express my gratitude to the EAC Secretariat and to all who had worked tirelessly to organize this Meeting. As we organise this twenty-sixth ordinary meeting of the Monetary Affairs Committee, it is important to recognise that it is the first time for some of us to take part in MAC meetings. Page 1 of 3 As Chairperson of the Committee, I would like to express a warm welcome and especially to whom is attending for the first time this important event, Honourable Emmanuel Tutuba, Governor Bank of Tanzania, and Honourable Johnny Ohisa Damian, Governor of Bank of South Soudan. Dear Colleagues Central Bank Governors, we are all aware that the global economy is experiencing recurrent shocks making the conduct of monetary policy very challenging. The lingering effects of Covid-19 coupled with the consequences of the war between Russia- Ukraine has affected the macroeconomic performances of our respective economies. These economic challenges harmed the attainment of monetary policy objective in general, and some macroeconomic convergence criteria. In such context, we must strengthen the cooperation and collaboration among policy makers to address the challenges that we are facing and to ensure a successful implementation of the Communitys goals for achieving our common objective. Ladies and Gentlemen, Distinguished Guests, Our community has made much progress with respect to the implementation of the Monetary Union Protocol, especially in terms of harmonization of regulatory framework, the adoption of the harmonized monetary and exchange policy framework, and fast tracking the macroeconomic convergence criteria,. These achievements are the fruit of hard work made by our former chairmen who provided good leadership and dedicated their efforts to the Community interest. I take this opportunity to extend my gratitude to Dr Patrick Njoroge, Governor of Central bank of Kenya for the accomplishment reached during his Chairmanship of MAC last year. He has closely followed the administrative procedures for the establishment of EAMI and we are aware for its operationalization to be effective. In this regard, it is important to fast track the operationalization of EAMI which is the keys institution to foster the harmonization of monetary and exchange rate policies, as well as strengthening coordination of operational and regulatory practices. We need to progress together as one, and, i would like to reiterate to the Governors to fast track the roadmap of implementation of protocol East African Monetary Union. During our meeting today, we will review the decisions and recommendations from the last meeting of MAC held in March 2022 and assess the progress of their implementation. Honourable Governors, distinguished Delegates, the Bank of the Republic of Burundi reiterates its commitment to the process of integration in East African Community and will share his experience of leadership on implementation of actions planned in the roadmap of establishment of East African Monetary Union. Page 2 of 3 I appreciated the work done by different MAC Technical Committees and I invite all the EAC Partner States Central Bank to continue enhancing collaboration and cooperation in the interest of achieving the EAC integration process. I wish this 26th MAC Meeting fruitful deliberations. Thank you. Page 3 of 3
